recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中大多為中大型原始細胞（blasts），核圓或略有凹摺、染色質細緻、部分可見小核仁，細胞質量少到中等、淡灰藍且無明顯顆粒，與少數成熟桿狀中性球並存；此形態可見於 ALL 也可見於單核球性白血病，必須靠流式或細胞化學區分。
features: Increased medium to large blasts with high N:C ratio
Round to indented/folded nuclei with fine, dispersed chromatin
Small nucleoli visible in some cells
Scant to moderate agranular pale gray-blue cytoplasm without Auer rods
Admixed small dark lymphocytes/erythroid precursors and occasional band neutrophils
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a predominance of medium to large blasts with high N:C ratios, round to indented nuclei, finely dispersed chromatin, occasional small nucleoli and scant to moderate agranular gray-blue cytoplasm. Auer rods are not seen, and there are scattered band neutrophils and small mature-appearing cells. The blasts lack definitive lineage-specific features. Morphology alone cannot distinguish lymphoblasts from monoblasts/promonocytes in this image; flow cytometry (CD19, CD10, cCD79a, CD34, TdT versus CD14, CD64, CD11b, lysozyme) and cytochemistry (MPO, nonspecific esterase) are required for classification.

ddx.vs: Monoblasts usually have more abundant gray-blue cytoplasm with fine vacuoles or granules, delicate nuclear folds and are nonspecific esterase positive and CD14/CD64 positive, while lymphoblasts are TdT and CD19 or cCD3 positive.
Minimally differentiated myeloblasts are morphologically similar but express CD13/CD33/CD117 and MPO by flow while lacking B- or T-lineage markers.
Hematogones have homogeneous condensed chromatin and scant cytoplasm and show a maturing CD10/CD20/CD34 continuum rather than a discrete blast population.
